newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mayor names Mary Loney new aviation chief.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mayor names Mary Loney new aviation chief.

text.p: Mary Rose Loney, the former aviation director for Philadelphia, will become Chicago's aviation commissioner effective Oct. 16, Chicago Mayor Richard Daley announced Monday.
Daley said he appointed Loney to the "critical position" of aviation commissioner because of her leadership skills and national reputation for effective management.

The mayor said Loney will oversee major projects planned at city airports such as a $130 million, bond-financed purchase of 365 acres of military land at O'Hare International airport that is slated for redevelopment, and a $500 million, bond-financed new terminal and parking facilities project at Midway Airport.
Loney comes to Chicago in the middle of a legal battle between the city and the state of Illinois over the planned closing of Meigs Field, a small airport on Chicago's downtown lakefront.
The Chicago Park District, which owns the airport land, plans to build a $27 million, bond-financed nature park on the site.

A U.S. District Court judge on Friday rejected a move by the state and a pilots group to block the airport's closing, scheduled for Monday night. That decision is expected to be appealed to U.S. Court of Appeals. Meanwhile, another lawsuit by the state that seeks to block the shutdown is pending in Cook County Circuit Court.
Loney said closing Meigs was "the right decision," and said she would work to accomodate users of the facility at the city's other airports.
Daley said the city would begin dismantling Meigs when a decision comes down "from an appropriate court."

Loney, who was appointed Philadelphia's aviation director in 1993, previously served as Chicago's first deputy aviation commissioner from 1989 to 1992. She replaces David Mosena, who became president of the Chicago Transit Authority earlier this year.
